Freshness and phase-failure controls remain separate from behavioral refinement. Monitoring/exploration review 2026-10-22: read-only daily freshness monitor and deterministic bounded schedules add evidence without changing model semantics, source-baseline policy or existing positive/mutation obligations. Model actions/invariants, regression commands, trace inventories and counterexample acceptance are unchanged; normal test checks remain mandatory. Participant inspection resolves existing profile evidence without approving keys or changing policy; display tests are separate from modeled semantics. Per-question pending resolution guard prevents same-tab double submission through stale controls; native browser regression preserves immutable fork/resolution rules. Patch 2.12.1 baseline/version fixtures preserve all upgrade and mismatch assertions. Signing journeys review 2026-10-22 (SPEC-002-051): task layout and explicit signer selection preserve Provider atomicity, generation invalidation, delivery guards and no unsigned fallback. Dialogue actions bind location/UUID and current model; awaited actions refuse changed models, while idle same-board refresh safely rebinds. Close during pending private-key import locks the Provider epoch; normal close retains a completed unlock. Exact-key approval now rechecks current disk/private-state evidence before mutation. Native browser regressions cover explicit signer choice, approval separate from possession, stale board operations, canceled import, focused edits and English/Polish geometry. These UI selection/dialogue states are executable-test coverage, outside the bounded Provider model; no universal refinement claim. Reviewed explicit evidence refresh: native reload and fixed-upload fresh Context validation do not approve a replacement; browser rotation regression retains the old approval and comparison draft. Pinned task navigation/focus/geometry is browser-tested presentation, outside the bounded model.

models.review: 2026-10-22: Reviewed source-bound immutable acceptance DAG, inherited winners, legacy explicit anchoring, eligibility blocking and author-only resolution against real reducer traces and unit/browser/CLI tests. Existing signing guard placement and exact-byte packet binding remain intact; first claim is inserted before signing. Reviewed explicit legacy anchoring, a third late offline claim and unauthorized-resolution mutation. Signed portable publication rechecks the exact question digest before each commit; browser delivery checks it against reviewed source bytes. Graph depth is measured using cached ancestor heights as well as traversal depth, so the 128-level refusal is independent of enumeration and memoization; both orders have boundary unit regressions. Reviewed demo/history comparisons and stale-submit regressions for read-only accepted questions, and exact 2.12 release/version/update fixtures; escape, immutable-history and duplicate-refusal assertions remain explicit. Verify older messages explicitly reprojects acceptance after eligibility changes, with current-board guards around the asynchronous refresh and a native 201-message-window regression. Signing clarity review 2026-10-22: readable display separates cryptographic signature integrity, local fingerprint approval, key lifecycle and existing eligibility. Participant inspection resolves existing profile evidence without approving keys or changing policy; display tests are separate from modeled semantics. Per-question pending resolution guard prevents same-tab double submission through stale controls; native browser regression preserves immutable fork/resolution rules. Patch 2.12.1 baseline/version fixtures preserve all upgrade and mismatch assertions. Read-only signing review 2026-10-22: session-local approval/removal re-evaluates already-verified affected messages using actual exact upload bytes and Context.evaluate; pending older evidence remains pending. Acceptance is reprojected from resulting eligibility without promoting history. Native test covers required-policy approval/removal; metadata/crypto/UI I/O remain outside this finite acceptance reducer model.

models.limits: Nine named immutable records, three root answers, one ordinary history message, one explicit legacy anchor, two concurrent resolutions and one merge; one reversible eligibility flag. Crypto, parsing/hash/source binding, UI/storage writes, arbitrary graph depth and general implementation refinement remain executable tests. Equal complete snapshots plus eligibility converge; disconnected first acceptance has explicit forks, never a global lock.
